'''John McKinley Chambers''' (born April 28, 1941) is the creator of the [[S (programming language)|S programming language]], and core member of the [[R (programming language)|R programming language]] project. He was awarded the 1998 [[ACM Software System Award]] for developing S.<ref name="acm">{{Cite web |url=http://www.acm.org/announcements/ss99.html |title=ACM honors Dr. John M. Chambers of Bell Labs with the 1998 ACM Software System Award for creating "S System" software |date=2008-09-21 |website=Association for Computing Machinery |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150827152522/https://www.acm.org/announcements/ss99.html |archive-date=2015-08-27 |access-date=2021-05-26 |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=John M. Chambers |url=https://awards.acm.org/award_winners/chambers_6640862 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250713115246/https://awards.acm.org/award_winners/chambers_6640862 |archive-date=2025-07-13 |access-date=2025-08-27 |website=Association for Computing Machinery Awards}}</ref>

==Early life==
John McKinley Chambers was born on April 28, 1941, in [[Toronto]], Ontario.<ref>{{cite book |title=American Men & Women of Science |date=2005 |editor-last1=Kalte |editor-first1=Pamela M. |editor-last2=Nemeh |editor-first2=Katherine H. |editor-last3=Schusterbauer |editor-first3=Noah |publisher=Gale Group |location=Detroit |isbn=978-0-7876-7392-5 |page=138 |edition=22 |url=https://archive.org/details/americanmenwomen0002unse_m9n5/page/138/mode/2up |via=[[Archive.org]]}}</ref> He received a [[Bachelor of Science]] from the [[University of Toronto]] in 1963. He received a [[Master of Arts]] in 1965 and a [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] degree in 1966, both in statistics, from [[Harvard University]].<ref name="acm"/><ref name="bell-cv">{{cite web |url=http://stat.bell-labs.com/jmc/vitae.html |title=John M. Chambers - Vitae |publisher=[[Bell Laboratories]] |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110707222829/http://stat.bell-labs.com/jmc/vitae.html |archive-date=2011-07-07}}</ref><ref name="stanford-cv">{{Cite web |url=http://statweb.stanford.edu/~jmc4/vitae.html |title=John M. Chambers - Vitae |website=Stanford University |access-date=2021-05-26}}</ref>

==Career==
Chambers started at [[Bell Laboratories]] in 1966 as a member of its technical staff.<ref name="acm"/><ref name="stanford-cv"/> From 1981 to 1983, he was the head of its Advanced Software Department and from 1983 to 1989 he was the head of its Statistics and Data Analysis Research Department.<ref name="acm"/><ref name="stanford-cv"/> In 1989, he moved back to full-time research and in 1995, he became a distinguished member of the technical staff.<ref name="acm"/><ref name="stanford-cv"/> In 1997, he was made the first [[Fellow]] of Bell Labs and was cited for "pioneering contributions to the field of statistical computing".<ref name="acm"/> He remained a distinguished member of the technical staff and a Fellow until his retirement from Bell Labs in 2005.<ref name="stanford-cv"/>

After retiring from Bell Labs, Chambers became a visiting professor at the [[University of Auckland]], [[University of California, Los Angeles]] and [[Stanford University]].<ref name="stanford-cv"/><ref>[https://statistics.stanford.edu/people/john-chambers Stanford University Department of Statistics Page for John M. Chambers.] Accessed January 16, 2010.</ref> Since 2008, he has been active at Stanford, currently serving as Senior Advisor of its [[data science]] program and an adjunct professor in Stanford's Department of Statistics.<ref name="stanford-cv"/>

Chambers is a Fellow of the [[American Statistical Association]], the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] and the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]].<ref name="stanford-cv"/><ref name="bell-cv"/>

==Awards and accomplishments==
Chambers has received the following awards:
* 1998, awarded the [[ACM Software System Award]] for developing the [[S (programming language)|S programming language]]. The award was presented on May 15, 1999.<ref name="acm"/>
* 2004, awarded an [[honorary degree|honorary]] Doctor of Mathematics degree from the [[University of Waterloo]]<ref name="stanford-cv"/>

===John M. Chambers Statistical Software Award===
Following his 1998 ACM Software System Award, Chambers donated his prize money (US$10,000) to the American Statistical Association to endow an award for novel statistical software, the ''John M. Chambers Statistical Software Award''.<ref name="chambers-award">{{cite web |url=http://stat-computing.org/awards/jmc/history.html |title=John M. Chambers Statistical Software Award. ASA Statistics Computing and Graphics }}</ref>
